images.title: Immeuble, 1 rue Le Peletier, Paris 9e
images.license: CC0 (Public Domain, Médiathèque de l'architecture et du patrimoine / Paris Musées)
images.author: Attribué à Paul Chevojon, photographe
images.street: 1, rue Le Peletier, Paris 9e (architect Georges Morin-Goustiaux)
images.shows: Full corner facade of an elaborate commercial/insurance building: a tall domed corner tourelle topped with an iron-crested finial, sculptural dormers, and a busy, varied roofline in place of a plain 45-degree attic — a strong example of the post-1884 discontinuity.

images.title: Castel Béranger, 14 rue La Fontaine
images.author: Greudin (Wikimedia Commons)
images.street: 14, rue La Fontaine, Paris 16e (architect Hector Guimard)
images.shows: Oblique full-facade view of Guimard's Castel Béranger: mixed brick/stone bays, sculptural iron balconies, and an irregular roofline with varied dormer forms.

images.title: Immeuble, 31 rue de Fleurus (album Ch. Girault)
images.license: CC0 (Public Domain, Médiathèque de l'architecture et du patrimoine / Paris Musées)
images.author: Albert Fernique, photographe
images.street: 31, rue de Fleurus, Paris 6e (architect Charles Girault; this print is filed within a Commons album titled "Immeuble avenue Henri Martin" but the photo itself is captioned 31 rue de Fleurus, Paris — the album appears to bundle several of Girault's works)
images.shows: Full corner facade in raking light: a tall, steep mansard/comble roof carrying multiple distinct dormer forms (round-headed, segmental, gabled), tall chimneys, a weathervane, and iron-cresting on the balcony railings — a clean discontinuity-test image.

images.title: Castel Béranger, upward facade view
images.author: Fred Romero
images.street: 14, rue La Fontaine, Paris 16e (architect Hector Guimard)
images.shows: Steep upward-angled view showing the roofline clearly: varied dormers, tall chimneys, and iron cresting along the parapet.

images.title: Castel Béranger entrance gate
images.author: Jean-Pierre Dalbéra
images.street: 14, rue La Fontaine, Paris 16e (architect Hector Guimard)
images.shows: Detail of the whiplash wrought-iron entrance gate and carved stone surround — evidence of the enriched decorative vocabulary of the period, not the roofline itself.

images.title: Immeuble Lavirotte, 29 avenue Rapp
images.author: Jean-Pierre Dalbéra
images.street: 29, avenue Rapp, Paris 7e (architect Jules Lavirotte; won the Ville de Paris facade competition)
images.shows: Full frontal facade of Lavirotte's masterpiece: sculpted dormers and iron cresting at the roofline over an exuberant ceramic and stone facade — a textbook discontinuity-test image.

images.title: 29 avenue Rapp, alternate view
images.author: Steve Cadman
images.shows: Alternate full-facade daylight view of the same building, confirming the roofline dormers and cresting from a different angle/lighting.

images.title: 29 avenue Rapp, roofline detail
images.author: Jean-Pierre Dalbéra
images.shows: Close detail of the upper comble zone: sculpted dormers, cresting figures, and ceramic ornament at the parapet — direct close-up evidence of the elaborated roofline.

images.title: Immeuble Les Arums, 33 rue du Champ de Mars
images.author: Jean-Pierre Dalbéra
images.street: 33, rue du Champ de Mars, Paris 7e (architect Octave Raquin; won the 1902 Ville de Paris facade competition)
images.shows: Full oblique facade with bow windows and dense floral art nouveau ornament in stone and iron; upper roofline partially visible at frame edge.

images.title: Les Arums, upper balcony detail
images.author: Jean-Pierre Dalbéra
images.street: 33, rue du Champ de Mars, Paris 7e (architect Octave Raquin)
images.shows: Detail of an upper-floor balcony with carved stone pediment ornament — evidences the enriched decorative program but does not itself show the comble roofline.

images.title: Immeuble, 130 rue Réaumur
images.author: MOSSOT
images.shows: Corner building with a domed corner tourelle and an elaborate mansard/comble roofline carrying multiple dormers and iron-crested balcony railings. Construction date not given in the Commons record; rue Réaumur was cut through in 1897 and most of its buildings date circa 1898-1905, so this is stylistically consistent with the family but the exact year is left blank rather than guessed.

notes: Corpus covers the 1884-1902 window via seven distinct buildings: two documentary-photograph archive prints with confirmed/approximate dates (1, rue Le Peletier 1899; 31 rue de Fleurus by Charles Girault, circa 1896) and five modern photographs of well-documented Art Nouveau immeubles (Castel Beranger 1895-98, 29 avenue Rapp/Lavirotte 1900-01, Les Arums/Champ de Mars circa 1900-02, 130 rue Reaumur undated). Rejected during vetting: a 'rue Piat' Commission du Vieux Paris photo (that program documented OLD buildings slated for demolition, not new construction, so it is not evidence for this family) and a 'percement de la rue Reaumur' photo (shows a building being demolished, not the new construction that replaced it). Coverage skews toward famous/landmark Art Nouveau immeubles because those are what have well-dated, high-quality Commons photography; more ordinary/modest post-1884 buildings are underrepresented since they are rarely individually documented on Commons with a confirmed construction date. The 130 rue Reaumur building's year is left blank per the no-guessing rule even though it is stylistically very likely in-period.
